what: Garmin makes GPS-based devices: running and diving watches, cycling computers, aviation avionics, marine chartplotters and in-car systems. Aviation and marine are smaller but far more profitable than consumer wearables.
customers: Runners, cyclists, divers and hikers; private aircraft owners and manufacturers; boat builders and boaters.
money: adventure watches, handhelds and satellite communicators
avionics for private and business aircraft
moat: Certified aviation avionics that take years to approve, and sports watches with an ecosystem of training data that users do not want to abandon.
risks: Apple competes directly in smartwatches with far greater scale
Auto OEM contracts are low-margin and concentrated
Tariffs affect a company that manufactures in Taiwan
opportunities: Revenue grew about 15% last year with a 26% operating margin
Aviation and marine give it high-margin businesses that consumer brands lack
Almost no debt: about $196 million against $2.3 billion of cash
watch: Outdoor and fitness segment growth and aviation order rates.
